message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Tests

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java-version: [8, 11, 17, 21, 25]
        clojure-version: ["1.12"]
        include:
          - java-version: 8
            clojure-version: "1.8"
          - java-version: 8
            clojure-version: "1.9"
          - java-version: 8
            clojure-version: "1.10"
          - java-version: 8
            clojure-version: "1.11"
          - java-version: 25
            clojure-version: "1.10"
          - java-version: 25
            clojure-version: "1.11"
    name: JDK ${{ matrix.java-version }}, Clojure ${{ matrix.clojure-version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java-version }}

      - uses: DeLaGuardo/setup-clojure@13.4
        with:
          lein: 2.11.2

      - uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.m2/repository
          key: m2-${{ matrix.java-version }}-${{ matrix.clojure-version }}-${{ hashFiles('project.clj') }}
          restore-keys: m2-${{ matrix.java-version }}-${{ matrix.clojure-version }}-

      - run: lein with-profile +${{ matrix.clojure-version }} test",
  "rationale": "The test job has no timeout, so a runaway job can consume unbounded runner time. Evidence pattern P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) and the P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT experiment (experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-a14b642d809bf336) support adding an explicit job timeout derived from successful history. The repository CI history shows successful runs completing in roughly 35-45 seconds, so a 5-minute job timeout provides operational headroom (including cold dependency installation) without removing any step, changing the matrix, or reducing build/test coverage. The dependency cache already exists (~/.m2/repository keyed by java-version, clojure-version, and project.clj), so P-LIT-GHA-CACHE is not applicable (equivalent cache present). Changing fail-fast to true is not applied because every matrix compatibility outcome across Java/Clojure versions is required, matching the P-LIT-FAIL-FAST contraindication that all matrix results are required and full failure diagnostics should be preserved.",
  "evidence_ids": ["P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-ishara-pattern-bat-a14b642d809bf336"]
}

- java 8 with clojure 1.12 (from product) plus includes: 1.8, 1.9, 1.10, 1.11 → so java 8 has clojure 1.12, 1.8, 1.9, 1.10, 1.11 = 5
- java 11 with clojure 1.12 = 1
- java 17 with clojure 1.12 = 1

fail-fast is false, meaning all 11 jobs run even if one fails.

The workflow is a test workflow; if it's a required check, canceling remaining matrix jobs might hide failures. However, the pattern says to evaluate the contract. The evidence is synthetic though (evidence scope: synthetic_fixture_on_dedicated_fork). The experiment examples have outcome scenario_passed but limitations say synthetic workload, not original repository CI savings.
